findings.title: parseBody after c.req.formData() reparses re-serialized body (CWE-436)
findings.why_it_matters: When anything has already called `c.req.formData()` on the request (a middleware inspecting a form field, for example), a later `c.req.parseBody()` no longer returns the same data. For urlencoded requests the field values are turned into new top-level keys: body `name=x%26role%3Dadmin%26y%3D` is seen by `formData()` as the single key `name`, but `parseBody()` now returns `{"------formdata-undici-...; name": ..., "role": "admin", "y": ...}`, so a caller can smuggle keys past a check done on the FormData view, and ordinary requests lose their real keys. For multipart requests `parseBody()` now throws `TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.` (unhandled, 500). At the base commit both cases returned the correct data because `parseBody` reused the cached FormData. The cause is that `arrayBuffer()` on a request whose only cached body is `formData` re-serializes that FormData as multipart with a fresh boundary, and those bytes are then parsed under the original Content-Type. Reusing `bodyCache.formData` when it is present, as `validator('form')` already does at validator.ts:115-116, removes the re-serialization entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: In `parseFormData` (src/utils/body.ts), reuse an existing cached FormData before touching the bytes, mirroring validator.ts:115-116: `if (request instanceof HonoRequest && request.bodyCache.formData) { return convertFormDataToBodyData<T>(await request.bodyCache.formData, options) }`, and only fall through to `arrayBuffer()` + `bufferToFormData()` when no FormData is cached. Add a test in src/request.test.ts that calls `req.formData()` then `req.parseBody()` for both urlencoded and multipart bodies.
evidence:
src/utils/body.ts:126-127 -- const arrayBuffer = await (request as Request).arrayBuffer()
  const formDataPromise = bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || '')

src/request.ts:228-234 -- const anyCachedKey = Object.keys(bodyCache)[0]; if (anyCachedKey) { return (bodyCache[anyCachedKey] as Promise<BodyInit>).then((body) => { ... return new Response(body)[key]() }) }  (with only `formData` cached, `new Response(formData).arrayBuffer()` yields multipart bytes with a new boundary)
Base behaviour, 9728702:src/utils/body.ts -- const formData = await (request as Request).formData()  (returns the cached FormData unchanged)

Scratch run on Node v24.21.0, base parseBody vs head parseBody against the same HonoRequest after `await r.formData()`: BASE urlencoded -> {"name":"x&role=admin&y="}; HEAD urlencoded -> {"------formdata-undici-030141752775
Content-Disposition: form-data; name":""name"

x","role":"admin","y":"
------formdata-undici-030141752775--
"}; BASE multipart -> {"name":"x"}; HEAD multipart -> THREW TypeError: Failed to parse body as FormData.
src/validator/validator.ts:115-116 -- if (c.req.bodyCache.formData) { formData = await c.req.bodyCache.formData }  (existing pattern that avoids the problem)

residual_risks: parseBody's new gate uses `split(';')[0].trim().toLowerCase()`; JS `trim()` strips more than HTTP whitespace (e.g. U+00A0, U+000B), so it accepts values the csrf middleware regex (`/^\b(application\/x-www-form-urlencoded|multipart\/form-data|text\/plain)\b/i`) does not treat as form submissions. On Node v24 this did not produce a CSRF bypass: such requests reach `Response.formData()`, which rejects the Content-Type, so the handler returns 500 instead of the previous `{}`; browsers also cannot send these values cross-site without a preflight. Not verified on Bun, Deno or workerd, whose `Response.formData()` MIME parsing may differ.

For HonoRequest, parseBody now keeps both the raw `arrayBuffer` and the parsed `formData` in `bodyCache` for the life of the request (previously only the FormData), roughly doubling retained memory for large multipart uploads on routes without the body-limit middleware. Not measured.
